input: Submit my photography to a local art competition

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing how many photos and which series or subject matter to enter determines the selection and curation effort required.
The specific competition — its name, host organisation, and deadline — drives every other step, including rules, format requirements, and timeline.
Entry fees, print costs, or equipment costs may affect how the submission is prepared and whether certain options are feasible.
Whether the user is submitting independently or with help (e.g. a mentor, print lab, or framer) changes what tasks they need to handle themselves.
Whether submission is digital upload, physical print, or both determines the preparation steps — file formatting, printing, framing, and delivery.
The user may have a preferred body of work or style they want to showcase, which guides photo selection and presentation choices.
Understanding whether the goal is winning, gaining exposure, getting feedback, or simply completing a first submission shapes how much polish and effort to invest.

gold.taskTitle: Submit photography to a local art competition
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to enter their photography into a local art competition, which involves selecting work, preparing submissions, and meeting entry requirements.

questions.title: Which specific competition are you entering, and when is the deadline?
questions.description: Identify the competition name, host organisation, and submission deadline to anchor the entire plan.

questions.title: How many photos are you allowed or planning to submit?
questions.description: Clarify the entry limit and how many pieces the user intends to enter, to scope the selection and preparation work.

questions.title: Is submission digital, physical prints, or both?
questions.description: Determine the delivery format required by the competition to define the correct preparation steps.

questions.title: What is your budget for entry fees, printing, and framing?
questions.description: Establish financial constraints that affect printing quality, framing choices, and whether all intended entries are feasible.

questions.title: Do you already know which photos you want to enter?
questions.description: Find out if the user has a curated selection in mind or needs help choosing from their portfolio.

questions.title: Will you be handling printing and framing yourself or using a service?
questions.description: Determine whether external vendors or helpers are involved, so the task list reflects only what the user must do personally.

questions.title: What does a successful submission look like to you — winning, exposure, or something else?
questions.description: Understand the user's primary goal to calibrate how much effort, polish, and strategy to build into the plan.
